newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government says no property briefing.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government says no property briefing.

text.p: Singapore's Ministry of National Development, dispelling market rumours of a news conference to announce new property market curbs, said on Tuesday it had no plans to hold a briefing.
"To my knowledge, the ministry has no plans to hold any press conference this week," a ministry spokesman told Reuters.
Market rumours said a news conference was planned for the weekend to announce a third set of curbs on the property market.

Property heavyweights like City Developments and Wing Tai Holdings have been battered to new 1997 lows of Singapore $11.40 and S$3.62 respectively on speculation the government would unveil more property curbs.
Among the rumours were plans to extend the compulsory holding period of public housing by between two to two-and-a-half years from the current five years.
The property index sank 17.23 points at noon on Tuesday to a new year low of 639.81, before rebounding slightly to 644.66 by 0720 GMT.
The rumours also hit banking stocks, sending UOB Foreign and Keppel Bank down to new year lows of S$13.20 and S$3.78 respectively.

The Singapore property market has seen two sets of curbs so far. The first was in May last year, aimed at speculators in the private housing sector and the second on April 12, targetted at at the public housing market.
